review.why: Sets pricing and packaging: first price, value metric, tiers, research methods, price increases with a staged rollout, and a pricing-page teardown.
review.summary: Starts with picking a first price you can learn from (about $10, $100 or $1,000 a month), then covers value metrics, good-better-best tiers, willingness-to-pay methods, signs it is time to raise prices and a staged rollout for existing customers. A pricing-page teardown scores clarity for human buyers and readability for AI agents.
strengths: Treats the first price as a bet to learn from, with a warning about ultra-low prices
Staged price-increase plan: test on new customers, then 5 to 10% of existing ones
Honest about the limits of survey methods such as Van Westendorp
cautions: Thresholds such as 40% conversion or 3% churn are rules of thumb
Models, tiers, research and teardown guides are in files not read here
